market.what: HFO and HFO-blend refrigerants (R-1234yf, R-454B, R-513A, R-1234ze...), world
market.method: Chemours Opteon $1.26B (2025) + Solstice/Honeywell similar (est. ~$1.2B) + Arkema, Daikin, China ~$0.5B; cross-check: R-1234yf alone $1.27B (2024 report)

value.logic: non-PFAS blend (R-32/R-152a/HC/CO2 class) taking 25% of ~$3B HFO at ~60% lower $/kg = ~$0.45B/yr; also avoids TFA (not counted)
value.revenue_logic: license blend patent to a gas maker; ~4% royalty on ~$125M blend sales at yr7 = ~$5M
value.margin_logic: license/royalty; blends of commodity gases, partner makes and sells

trend.drivers: AIM Act + EU F-gas 2024/573 shift to low GWP; EU PFAS/TFA concern; but EU study suggests refrigerants may be exempted
trend.deadline: EU F-gas: GWP<150 in many split ACs/heat pumps from 2027; PFAS decision ~2027

competition.notes: incumbents own most blend patents; natural refrigerants (R-290, R-744) are the default non-PFAS route; solid-state cooling startups raised large rounds

lab.synth: catalog: blend of known gases (no new molecule; new molecules would need $1M+ tox for ASHRAE 34)
lab.test: flammability ASTM E681, VLE/glide, drop-in capacity and COP in a psychrometric/calorimeter rig (AHRI 210/240 or SAE J2765) at an HVAC test lab
lab.logic: blend modeling 2 wk + E681 3 wk + rig 6 wk; gases ~$3k + E681 ~$15k for 3 blends + rig rental ~$60k (est.)

sale.gates: ASHRAE 34 / ISO 817 number ~1 yr; EPA SNAP 1-2 yrs; IEC/UL 60335-2-40 charge limits; OEM qual 2-3 yrs (MAC 3-5)
